expectations.text: Hero headline leads with outcome/impact, not project name or 'Redesigning...'
expectations.evidence: The h1 reads: 'How a unified inventory dashboard cut stock-outs by 45% and saved store managers 90+ minutes daily' - leads directly with the impact metrics and outcome.

expectations.text: At least 2 key metrics displayed prominently in hero section (45% drop, 90min saved, 340 stores)
expectations.evidence: Three metric cards displayed prominently in hero section: 45% stock-out reduction, 90+ min time saved, 340+ store adoption.

expectations.text: Uses first-person ownership language ('I led', 'I conducted', 'I designed') not passive voice
expectations.evidence: Multiple instances: 'I started by embedding myself', 'I conducted six in-depth interviews', 'I spent a full day', 'I worked closely', 'I proposed', 'I iterated', 'I tested three patterns'.

expectations.text: Does not explicitly claim 'senior designer' or 'senior level' - lets work speak
expectations.evidence: Role described as 'Solo Designer' with date context. No seniority claims. The work scope and outcomes let the seniority speak implicitly.

expectations.text: Explicitly mentions the product is live/in production and used by real users
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states: 'The feature has been live since October 2024 and is actively used by 340+ stores' and 'checking the dashboard is now the first thing they do at the start of their shift'.

expectations.text: Problem section addresses user pain AND business impact, not just UI issues
expectations.evidence: Problem section covers: user pain (2+ hours reconciling inventory, no contextual intelligence), business impact (stock-out incidents frequent/reactive, support team burden, regional manager issues), and technical challenges.

expectations.text: Research section explains WHY specific methods were chosen, not just listing them
expectations.evidence: Discovery section explains 'Rather than relying on second-hand reports, I wanted to see inventory management in context' and explains the insight reframed the challenge from data overload to information fragmentation and lack of predictive capability.

expectations.text: Output is valid TypeScript/Next.js component with proper exports
expectations.evidence: Valid component export: metadata object with Metadata type, default export function, proper Next.js structure with Image import and semantic article element.
Uses responsive classes throughout: grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3, text-4xl sm:text-5xl, px-6 sm:px-8, py-20 sm:py-32. Mobile-responsive view mentioned explicitly in solution.

expectations.text: Uses semantic HTML elements (article, section, figure)
expectations.evidence: Uses <article>, <section> elements throughout. Properly structured semantic HTML with meaningful heading hierarchy (h1, h2).
